30 ======= How long each post stays on screen before the rotation moves on, in seconds — the pace of the whole widget, and a resource so a build can retune it without a code change.
TWENTY, and the reasoning is about a glance rather than about a clock. Five posts at this interval come round in a hundred seconds, so somebody who unlocks their phone a few times an hour sees a different post nearly every time — which is the entire point of the request this exists to answer. It is also four times the few seconds it takes to read a headline and a byline, so the card does not change while it is being read. Under about ten seconds it would, and it would spend a wake-up every few seconds to do it; over thirty, a single unlock usually misses any movement at all.
IT IS A REQUEST, NOT A GUARANTEE. `PostsRotationWorker` is one-time WorkManager work with an initial delay, so JobScheduler batching, Doze and the app-standby buckets all get a say: with the screen on and the app in an active bucket the real cadence lands around this number, and in a `rare` or `restricted` bucket it can stretch to minutes. That is correct platform behaviour and the widget does not fight it — no exact alarms.
`PostsRotationWorker` clamps whatever is written here into 5 … 300 seconds, so an override cannot turn this into a wake-up loop or something slower than the refresh tick it exists to beat. --> 20 >>>>>>> eb94101b (chore: sync latest frontend/backend changes)
